reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a Borel measurable structure. For arbitrary measures nu and reference on E x E,any xstar in E and real kappa,r,Mx,Mp,assume kappa>=1. Write
  Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2,
  P_kappa(nu,reference)=inf_{pi coupling of nu,reference}
                          integral^- ENNReal.ofReal(Q_kappa(s-sprime)) dpi.
Assume the real functions (X,P)->||X-xstar||^2 and (X,P)->||P||^2 are separately Bochner integrable under reference,and
  integral ||X-xstar||^2 dreference <= Mx,
  integral ||P||^2 dreference <= Mp,
  P_kappa(nu,reference) <= ENNReal.ofReal(r^2).
Then the real function (X,P)->||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2 is Bochner integrable under nu,and
  integral (||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2) dnu <= 2(Mx+Mp)+24r^2.
Both measures are arbitrary,with no probability normalization assumption. r,Mx,Mp are arbitrary real parameters without separately stated nonnegativity assumptions. xstar is any vector,not a stationary point supplied by a potential. The phase moment is the explicit sum of coordinate squared norms,not the square of the default maximum product norm. The transport input is the unrooted quadratic phase cost with specified marginals;no sampled-state or iteration-history interpretation is part of this theorem.
